title: Analyst, Market Optimization & Trading
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Energy Management, the Analyst, Market Optimization & Trading, will support the development and execution of trading, hedging, and optimization strategies for Clearway’s ERCOT and PJM assets. The Analyst will work in close coordination with the Market Optimization & Trading, Market Fundamentals, Business Development, Origination, Asset Management, Credit and Energy Risk, and Operations groups to help manage Clearway’s market exposure while building deep expertise in nodal power market analytics within a rapidly growing organization.

If you do not meet 100% of the below qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Support the development and execution of day-ahead, real-time, and term trading and hedging strategies for Clearway’s ERCOT and PJM assets, including energy, ancillary services, and basis positions.
  • Assist in identifying and analyzing congestion market risk, including congestion.
  • Support participation in CRR/FTR auctions and virtual bidding strategies.
  • Work with Credit and Energy Risk to support the internal approval process for trading counterparties and transactions.
  • Communicate with project stakeholders on market conditions, trading risks, and optimization opportunities.
  • Work with the Market Analytics and Credit and Energy Risk teams to develop and enhance tools for position management, reporting, trade capture, and the eventual implementation of an enterprise risk management system.
  • Develop, operate, and maintain production cost and price forecasting models (e.g., using tools such as UPLAN, PROMOD, or Dayzer) to support nodal price and congestion forecasting for ERCOT and PJM.
  • Leverage data to create tools and automate workflows.
  • Mark and maintain forward price curves for ERCOT and PJM power products, and support stochastic risk modeling and correlation assumptions.
  • Prepare recurring and ad-hoc market recaps, outlooks, and presentation materials summarizing ERCOT and PJM fundamentals, price drivers, and trading performance for internal stakeholders.
  • Support day-to-day position management and P&L reporting for ERCOT and PJM trading portfolios.
  • Oversee the Energy Management documentation process, leveraging Clearway’s internal and external subject matter experts to bring trading, ISO, QSE, and enabling agreements to execution.
  • Participate in energy working groups, professional organizations, trade shows & conferences.
  • Track and report on ERCOT and PJM policy and regulatory developments, including ISO market rule changes, that may impact trading strategy, leveraging Clearway’s internal and external subject matter experts.
  • Ability to travel up to 25% of the time.
  • Maintain confidentiality and sensitivity with respect to all functions of Clearway.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, business administration, engineering, economics, mathematics, meteorology, or a related quantitative field.
  • 0-2 years of relevant experience
  • Strong analytical and quantitative skills with a curious, inquisitive mindset and a genuine drive to understand how power markets work. Prior trading experience is not required – relevant coursework, internship, or academic research in a quantitative field will also be considered.
  • Interest in or exposure to ERCOT and/or PJM market structure, including day-ahead and real-time markets, CRR/FTRs, and ancillary services, is a plus but not required.
  • Solid understanding of power markets, including forwards, futures, swaps, and options.
  • Ability to extract, manipulate, and analyze large datasets relevant to energy markets to support trading and risk decisions.
  • Proficiency with Python, SQL, or other coding/statistical tools is a plus.
  • Highly motivated, self-starter, friendly personality, and good team player.
  • Attention to detail and inclination towards structure, organization, and process – as well as the ability to examine, question, and improve on the inputs and recommendations of others.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to oversee multiple projects simultaneously, track progress and needs of each, and provide high-quality deliverables accurately and on time.
  • Able to work well with geographically dispersed, cross-functional teams in a fast-paced environment.
  • Highly proficient in Microsoft Excel; proficient in Word and PowerPoint.

title: Analyst, Procurement
description:
What The Role Is

This role supports competitive sourcing and procurement execution for battery energy storage system (BESS) equipment. This role assists with RFx development and administration, bid evaluations, supplier communications, and preparation of award recommendations, while coordinating across internal stakeholders (Development, Engineering, Legal, Finance, Construction, and Operations) to advance supplier selection, contracting, and purchase order execution. The Analyst will support ongoing contract administration activities, maintaining documentation and trackers, and contributing market intelligence related to suppliers, logistics, tariffs, and policy changes that may impact project cost and schedule.

This position will report to the Senior Manager, Procurement, and can be hybrid-based in Scottsdale, AZ, or Denver, CO offices.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Support the Senior Manager, Procurement, and category leads in executing sourcing strategies and procurement activities for equipment focused primarily on BESS equipment
  • Administer competitive RFx processes for BESS equipment, including drafting RFx packages, managing Q&A, coordinating bid submissions, and maintaining bidder lists and timelines
  • Support supplier evaluation by organizing technical and commercial inputs, documenting clarifications, and helping assess risks and opportunities (commercial terms, schedule, warranty, logistics, and bankability considerations)
  • Perform bid evaluations and scenario analyses in Excel to evaluate pricing, inclusions/exclusions, assumptions, and key cost drivers; track and report cost movements throughout negotiations
  • Support negotiations by preparing redlines/issue trackers, summarizing supplier responses, and highlighting cost, schedule, and commercial risks for internal review
  • Coordinate cross-functionally to support alignment between BESS equipment agreements and related project documents, including EPC agreements, offtake agreements, interconnection, O&M/service agreements, warranties, logistics plans, and commissioning responsibilities
  • Assist with scope reviews to help identify gaps, interfaces, and owner-furnished versus contractor-furnished responsibilities for BESS equipment packages
  • Support vendor relationship management by scheduling recurring business review meetings and ad-hoc working sessions, documenting decisions and action items, tracking progress toward commercial milestones and deliverables, and recording product roadmap updates.
  • Orchestrate and lead the Procurement and Engineering organization’s technology and cost forecasting reporting by gathering and summarizing market and commercial intelligence across all owner-furnished equipment categories (including BESS, solar, and wind)
  • Orchestrate monthly reporting by coordinating within the Procurement organization to gather pricing, technology, and sourcing inputs across departments
  • Conduct periodic market intelligence, commodity, and pricing assessments and reporting impacting OFE and EPC sourcing efforts
  • Maintain sourcing workplans, bidder qualifications, and internal trackers to support timely vendor selection
  • Coordinate with internal stakeholders to compile inputs, track open items, and support the timely resolution of questions related to equipment scope, schedule, and commercial terms
  • Perform ad hoc analyses related to equipment sourcing, market intelligence analyses, or continuous improvement opportunities identified within the department
  • Support internal reviews of material changes and deviations to standard terms by preparing summaries, tracking approvals, and maintaining version control of supplier proposals and draft agreements
  • Coordinate with Engineering to gather and maintain BESS equipment specifications, technical requirements, and documentation needed for RFx packages and contracting
  • Maintain organized procurement files and correspondence to ensure documentation is complete and audit-ready
  • Support project financing diligence by coordinating inputs and responses related to BESS equipment scope, warranties, testing, and delivery schedules
  • Provide procurement team support as needed across adjacent categories, including EPC interfaces, balance-of-plant equipment, and O&M/services, while maintaining primary focus on BESS equipment sourcing and contracting
  • Assist in the development and implementation of procurement templates, tools, and processes (RFx templates, bid tabs, trackers, and playbooks), including the incorporation of continuous improvement opportunities

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in economics, finance, procurement and supply chain, engineering, or related field
  • 1-2 years of experience in procurement, sourcing, contracts administration, project development, battery storage engineering, or a related role
  • Experience supporting RFx processes, bid evaluation/levelization, or supplier management for equipment and/or construction-related scopes (energy, industrial, or infrastructure preferred)
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to summarize commercial terms, track issues, and support contract reviews and negotiations
  • Ability to travel up to 10%
  • Proficient in Microsoft SharePoint, Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), OneNote, and document control

What Would Be Nice

  • Experience with BESS equipment supply agreements and an understanding of key commercial terms (warranty, performance guarantees, liquidated damages, logistics, and commissioning/test requirements)
  • Familiarity with battery/PCS supplier landscape and drivers such as lead times, domestic content requirements, tariffs, and shipping constraints
  • Experience supporting utility-scale renewables or energy storage projects, including coordination with engineering and construction stakeholders

title: Assistant Project Manager Pre-Construction, Solar-BESS
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Pre-Construction Director, the Assistant Project Manager Pre-Construction, Solar-BESS works with the Development, Engineering, and Procurement teams during early-, middle-, and late-stage Development Projects, bringing a Construction perspective. The Assistant Project Manager Pre-Construction, Solar-BESS will review project studies and designs, engineering-procurement-construction schedules, Owner Furnished Equipment deliveries, construction feasibility and risk, environmental compliance, budgets, safety plans, quality plans, contract terms and exhibits, and project finance requirements. This person will represent the Construction Team until handoff to the Construction Project Manager at Full Notice to Proceed.

This position will be based in the San Francisco, Scottsdale, Denver, or San Diego office.

If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume

What You'll Be Doing

  • Early Design and Site Feasibility: Review site and early designs for feasibility and efficiency via desktop and site visits. Identify traffic patterns, access, existing topography and soils characteristics, vegetation and trees to remove, potential protected biology and cultural resources, watercourses, wetlands, neighbors, safety and security concerns, and interconnection access.
  • Schedule Analysis and Development: Review and provide input on assumed schedule timelines for RFP process, Engineering and Procurement durations, Construction, and Commissioning timelines to Guaranteed Milestones. Work with Procurement group to coordinate Owner Furnished Equipment schedule deliveries with EPC.
  • Construction Risk: Evaluate site for risks related to access to Interconnection Facilities, neighbors and context, site access and transportation, vegetation, existing structures to demolish, security and safety requirements, temporary facilities and O&M building location, water availability, geological and hydrological considerations, soil red flags, weather impacts, dust control requirements, Fire Department Requirements, and Labor requirements.
  • Project Budget Review: Provide input on Owner’s overall project budget including EPC costs, Owner’s Construction Management costs, Per Diem requirements, and cost of key risks to be incorporated into Contingency.
  • Safety Planning and Review: Review potential EPC Site Specific Safety Plan for adherence to Clearway Energy standards. Review and negotiate safety-related terms in EPC contract and Exhibits. Relay final requirements to Clearway Safety and Construction Execution team prior to Full Notice to Proceed.
  • EPC Contract Term and Exhibit negotiation: Review, redline, and negotiate EPC Agreement Terms related to Scope of Work, Contractor Deliverable formats, Safety Requirements, Operational Spare Parts, Payment Application-Schedule of Values-Cash flow, Quality Assurance, Liquidated Damages, and Guaranteed Milestone requirements.
  • Utility Interconnection Support: Track Utility upgrade timelines to grid synchronization and ensure EPC High Voltage scope is properly coordinated. Act as Liaison to the Construction High Voltage and Commissioning Team before construction.
  • Commissioning Team coordination: Understand and review EPC Agreement Terms and Contract Exhibits around un-energized and energized testing, commissioning, and Performance Testing. Act as Liaison to Construction Commissioning Team before construction.
  • Prevailing Wage, Labor, and Apprenticeship requirements: Identify requirements for Project Labor Agreements, Prevailing Wage, and Apprenticeship programs. Ensure scope and cost included in EPC contract and relay requirements to Execution team prior to Full Notice to Proceed.
  • Pre-Work Agreement Budget Management: Review and craft PWA’s with Procurement Team, review and approve monthly invoices ensuring conformance with pre-construction cash flow schedule, collect and maintain Lien Waivers for Financial Close.
  • Day-to-Day: Flexibility required to prioritize and support multiple projects simultaneously to track to EPC readiness at Financial Close. Communicate with Pre-Construction Team daily on project status towards key milestones including RFP release, EPC Contract Execution, and Full Notice to Proceed.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Provide project updates to Pre-Construction Team and upstream leadership, participate in Development Monthly Meetings, and support documents requesting capital spend approval.

What You'll Bring

  • HS Diploma or GED is required
  • Renewable Energy construction, engineering, or project management experience
  • 3-5 years of experience with Commercial or Utility Solar Energy or Battery projects.
  • Experience working for an EPC Construction Contractor, CM Consulting Firm, Engineering Firm, or Owner/Developer.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with complex internal and external teams, building consensus and driving project and corporate initiatives
  • Experience working with Utilities, Developers, Engineers, and EPC Contractors.
  • Proven experience in project development, design and engineering, and construction with a focus on renewable energy solar and battery projects.
  • Knowledge of solar and battery energy systems, development practices, and construction processes.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills to manage multiple tasks and priorities.
  • Proficiency in project management software and tools.
  • Strong critical thinking abilities to identify critical risks and fatal flaws.
  • Effective communication skills to liaise with diverse teams and stakeholders.
  • Willingness to work onsite and travel as required.

What Would Be Nice

Reporting to the Wind Site Lead, the Evening Shift Wind Technician is responsible for assisting in the performance of wind turbine mechanical, hydraulic, and electric component maintenance. The primary objective is to maintain safe, effective, efficient, and profitable wind turbine operation.

Wind Technician levels are defined below, and the ranges will be determined based on the qualifications met.

Wind Technician I ($45,000 - $66,000)

  • Follow safety procedures, observe safe working practices and maintain a safe working environment.
  • Assist in the performance of wind turbine mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical component maintenance.
  • Documents all work performed, parts used and time spent using computer based service reporting procedures.
  • Assist in troubleshooting and repair of SCADA communication systems.
  • Operate and maintain a service vehicle.
  • Maintain hand tools in good working order and well organized.

  • Able to create, edit or modify Microsoft Word and Excel documents.
  • Able to meet the requirements of Clearway Energy Group’s Qualified Electrical Worker program.

  • An Associate’s degree (electrical or technical) and six months turbine experience, or a high school diploma/GED and one-year wind turbine experience
  • Able to work with electrical wires and differentiate between color coded wires.
  • Have an in depth understanding of the different components of the wind turbine including the electrical pitch system, computerized control system, and the power conversion unit as well as knowledge and understanding of OEM approved mechanical maintenance methods and practices.
  • Possess the skills to perform mechanical and electrical equipment repairs.

title: High Voltage Technician
description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Manager, the High Voltage Technician will oversee the operation, maintenance, and repair of MV & HV electrical equipment for wind energy projects. This person must possess a minimum of five years’ experience in the troubleshooting, repair and maintenance of high voltage systems at a power generating facility, or similar industrial setting.

This position will be located at our Alta site in Mojave, CA.

If you don’t meet 100% of the below qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Support high voltage maintenance and troubleshooting. Ensure compliance to national/local electrical standards and company objectives.
  • Review, assist and/or perform high voltage switching, and grounding using approved switching orders and procedures.
  • Service, troubleshoot and repair high voltage collective systems, including overhead power lines, underground cable systems, substation switching equipment, power instrumentation and transformer equipment up to 230KV.
  • Instruct, train, and assist site personnel in safe work practices. Ensure compliance with industry safe work practices by wind site employees and contractors performing Balance of Plant work activities.
  • Review specific work for site planned outages. Ensure work includes time based or condition-based maintenance. Verify the availability/accuracy of permits, LOTOs, contractors, test equipment, repair parts and tools.
  • Be onsite during planned outages to assist and supervise as needed. Follow contractor work progress. Ensure unsatisfactory test results/conditions recorded are resolved, verified and addressed before contractor demobilization and restoration of equipment.
  • Track site discrete relay calibration due dates for assigned sites. Supervise the implementation of Company procedures by contracted testing personnel. Review and file final relay test reports.
  • Ensure modifications made to site equipment are documented for future reference. Maintain test logs.
  • Review site-specific equipment manuals for maintenance and repair requirements.
  • Maintain log books, work orders, procedures, timesheets, expense reports, requisitions and other documentation as required.
  • Work alternate shift schedule on short term basis and overtime as required.

What You'll Bring

  • Must possess a high school diploma or GED
  • Five years of relevant experience is required
  • Completion of a formal apprenticeship program or equivalent combination of work experience and technical training required

    Knowledge & Skills

    • Must have an understanding of electrical power generation, distribution, and possess a thorough knowledge of MV and HV systems including overhead, underground and substation systems.
    • Must possess a good understanding of operating procedures, environmental and safety rules and regulations, and first aid procedures.
    • Must possess a valid driver’s license – Class B, or Class A preferred.

    Must be skilled in:

    • The use of a variety of electrical test equipment and hand tools
    • Interpreting and following technical instruction furnished in verbal, written, diagrammatic and schedule formats
    • Reading and interpreting electrical drawings, technical manuals, and test reports
    • Using test gauges, digital multi-meters, oscilloscopes, and specialized test equipment to test overhead, underground, and substation equipment

    Specific areas of knowledge/familiarity:

    • NFPA 70E and Arc Flash hazards

description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Wind Site Manager, the Lead Technician will contribution to the day to day operations of the Lookout wind site, by participating in and monitor the performance of wind turbine mechanical, hydraulic, and electric component maintenance and sub-station activities. The primary objective of this position is to maintain safe, effective, efficient, and profitable wind turbine operations.

If you don’t meet 100% of the below qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

  • Monitor, abide by and enforce safe work practices as they relate to wind plants, wind plant personnel, wind turbine repairs, maintenance, and balance of plant activities
  • Inspect completed repairs and scheduled maintenance for quality assurance
  • Troubleshoot complicated mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical problems on Clearway owned equipment

  • Use proper tooling and equipment to perform troubleshooting, repair and maintenance activities on Clearway owned equipment
  • Support in all areas of site operations, including leading crews, as directed by Site Manager and with minimal supervision

  • Responsible for updating manuals, work instructions and technical wind turbine data
  • Read and understand electrical schematics and wiring diagrams and mentor others as needed
  • Monitor site conditions, contractors, and Clearway personnel to maximize revenue and minimize downtime during repairs and maintenance
  • Ensure crews maintain all tools and equipment in good working order and well organized
  • Safely perform LOTO and mentor lower level technicians in LOTO
  • Perform balance of plant, O&M facility and switchyard maintenance, repairs, and inspection as required
  • Work a flexible schedule, including weeknights, weekends, and holidays as needed
  • Ensure all vehicles and equipment are properly maintained and serviced

What You'll Bring

  • High school diploma or GED is required
  • Associates degree (electrical or technical) and 2+ years turbine experience, or 5+ years wind turbine experience required

  • Comfortable standing outside the nacelle and nosecone at the top of the turbine and working in adverse weather conditions

Reporting to the Director of Business Development and M&A, the role is responsible for growing the Clearway development and operating platform for utility-scale wind, solar, and energy storage projects, as well as multi-technology complexes. Alternatively, the candidate may bring similar and transferable experience from an investment banking firm.
  • Comfort navigating transactions, particularly the negotiation of M&A transactions.

  • Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with internal and external customers at all levels.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Proficient with Microsoft Office applications, including performing financial and analytical computations in Excel.
  • Detail-oriented and adaptable to changing working requirements.

  • Demonstrate a “can-do” attitude in embracing company goals and initiatives.

description:
What The Role Is

As a key member of the West Business Development & M&A team, the Senior Analyst will support commercial strategy and investment decisions across utility-scale wind, solar, and battery storage assets. The role will combine development underwriting and PPA bidding with buy-side and sell-side M&A execution, including valuation, financial modeling, diligence, and transaction materials. This position reports directly to the Director, Business Development & M&A.

The role will be primarily focused on CAISO, Hawaii, and other West markets, while also supporting cross-region strategic M&A, including portfolio, operating, opportunistic acquisition, and asset-sale processes. This role is primarily focused on markets in California and Hawaii but will collaborate regularly with colleagues covering the broader West region.

This position is based in our Denver office; however, San Francisco-based candidates will be considered as an exception on a case-by-case basis for the right candidate.

If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Build and own financial models for renewable energy projects. Evaluate project economics, returns, and key risks, working closely with Development, Engineering, Capital Markets, and other teams. Run sensitivities and identify ways to improve project value.
  • Evaluate acquisition and sale opportunities. Build and manage acquisition models for operating projects, development assets, and portfolios, and drive valuation analyses and operating/financing sensitivities.
  • Partner alongside M&A deal leads on several core work streams for live transactions, including review of target company information, coordination of Q&A process and management of due diligence effort across internal subject matter experts and external consultants.
  • Prepare detailed memos and presentations for senior management and investment committee.
  • Support ongoing origination, development, and financing activities for projects:
    • Support pricing analysis and bidding strategy to originate offtake contracts for Clearway Energy Group’s 25GW+ development portfolio of utility wind, solar, and storage projects
    • Develop statistical analyses to quantify risk in highly structured transactions
    • Perform quantitative and qualitative analysis to work out impediments to negotiations and closings
    • Work with functional groups, third-party consultants, and various other stakeholders to drive projects forward and perform quantitative analyses to support development and financing judgements.
  • Oversee the integration of acquired projects into Clearway’s operating fleet, coordinating with relevant teams to ensure seamless transition and operation.
  • Develop and maintain internal tools and processes for tracking all active, inactive, and closed M&A deal activities.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor's Degree with a strong academic record from an undergraduate program, ideally with focus in economics, finance, or business administration.
  • 2+ years of relevant work experience, project finance, corporate finance, consulting, strategy, corporate development, renewable energy, or a related analytical field.
  • A demonstrated interest in renewable energy projects and/or electricity markets in the United States is preferred.
  • Aptitude for analytical and financial modeling with demonstrated attention to detail. Advanced capabilities in Excel, Word, and PowerPoint are essential.
  • Experience or demonstrated curiosity integrating AI tools into analytical and deal workflows.
  • Strong oral, written, and visual communication skills. Ability to summarize complex issues and identify opportunities or next steps is critical.

  • Ability to manage simultaneous projects/work streams, set priorities, and exercise judgment independently.
  • Interest in developing management skills and desire to grow personally and professionally within our organization.

Reporting to the Maintenance Manager, the Solar Technician is responsible for troubleshooting, maintaining, servicing, and repairing solar PV systems and associated equipment. The primary objective is to maintain safe, effective, efficient, and profitable solar PV operation.

If you don’t meet 100% of the below qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

Pay Ranges by Job Level:

Technician Trainee ($50,000 - $60,000)

Solar Technician I ($54,000 - $77,000)

Solar Technician II ($62,000 - $88,000)

Solar Technician III ($88,000 - $107,000)

Trainee

  • Follow safety procedures, observe safe working practices, and maintain a safe working environment under direct supervision.
  • Shadow and assist experienced technicians in the performance of PV systems and electrical component maintenance.
  • Maintain hand tools in good working order and well organized.
  • Operate and maintain a service vehicle.
  • Work a flexible on-call schedule when needed. This may include weeknights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Demonstrate a strong willingness to learn and accept guidance from supervising technicians and site leadership.
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Other duties as assigned within the Trainee scope.

  • Willingness to progress as a technician and take guidance from superiors.
  • Help in all areas of site operations as directed by Site Lead and Site Manager with minimal supervision
  • Ensures work is performed in accordance with Environmental and Safety requirements.
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level I scope

Level II (Additions)

  • Performs corrective, preventive, and emergency maintenance and operations for which they are qualified to safely and efficiently perform
  • Performs work independently and/or in work crews
  • Must pass an advancement exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Travel required as needed
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level II scope

Level III (Additions)

  • Executes routine electrical troubleshooting and repair, instrumentation calibration and troubleshooting
  • Performs complex maintenance work such as distributed control systems and inverter troubleshooting as assigned by supervisor based on level of skill and ability
  • Complete work orders for the preventive maintenance management system
  • Performs corrective, preventive, and emergency maintenance on all PV Solar equipment
  • Prepares and implements switching and clearance orders, while working with Operations Center
  • Operates all electrical and mechanical PV Solar power plant systems
  • Participates in training as required, JHA, PJB, LOTO documentation
  • Writes Plant Orders, Plant Procedures, Operating Instructions and other documents as assigned by supervisor
  • Ensures work is performed in accordance with Environmental and Safety requirements
  • Must pass an exam and oral board upon training program completion within six (6) months from hire.
  • Performs other duties as assigned within the level III scope

What You'll Bring

Trainee

  • A high school diploma or GED required, or willing to obtain within the first 6 months of employment.
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license and good driving record.
  • Demonstrable mechanical aptitude; no prior electrical experience required.
  • Able to safely work in a wide range of adverse climates and environments.
  • Able to travel as required.
  • Knowledge of and the ability to use various hand tools.
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing.
  • Able to create, edit, or modify Microsoft Word and Excel documents.
  • Ability to work overtime and non-standard working hours (nights, holidays, weekends), when needed.
  • Professionalism and excellent communication skills.

Level I

  • Possess demonstrable mechanical aptitude and basic electrical knowledge gained through direct work experience. Qualifying backgrounds include: electrical work in a construction trade, employment in a power generation or utility environment, or experience as a licensed or apprentice electrician. Able to work with electrical wires and differentiate between color-coded wires.
  • Understanding of general workplace safety and the ability to follow safety standards, as well as help the company improve upon the standards in place.
  • Ability to read schematics and wiring diagrams is preferred.
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing and able to work without direct supervision during performance of work.
  • Able to meet the requirements of Clearway Energy Group’s Qualified Electrical Worker program.
  • Knowledge of applicable safety and environmental regulations.
  • Able to work both independently and as part of a multi-tasking team.

Level II (Additions)

  • 1+ years of experience in a power plant or PV Solar O&M/EPC experience
  • 2+ years of field experience with significant I&E, I&C and/or C&I Electrician experience will be considered in lieu of applicable solar experience
  • Demonstrated knowledge of electrical or mechanical fundamentals (single craft journeyman skills) such as electrical measurements, control circuits, and solid state theory application
  • Basic knowledge of operational characteristics of equipment and associated control devices installed in power facilities
  • Possess demonstrable mechanical aptitude and basic electrical knowledge

Level III (Additions)

  • 4+ years of PV solar experience is required. I&E, I&C and/or C&I Electrician experience will be considered in lieu of applicable experience.
  • Proven experience with a multitude of electrical/construction projects
  • Demonstrated knowledge of electrical or mechanical fundamentals (Journeyman skills) such as electrical measurements, control circuits, and solid state theory application
  • Knowledge of complex analog and digital instrumentation and control systems
  • Proper methods for troubleshooting, repairing, and adjusting instruments and control systems
  • Experience administering safe methods to clear equipment, use of tools and plant safety rules
  • Understanding reporting procedures and practices and maintenance procedures and practices
  • Knowledge of electrical and mechanical prints
  • Familiarity with PV Solar plant terminology and nomenclature
  • Qualified to perform routine and emergency operations at a solar generation facility and Switchyard
  • Able to communicate verbally and in writing and able to work without direct supervision during performance of work
  • Able to travel (approximately 5%)

What Would Be Nice

  • 2-year technical degree or equivalent Journeyman certification/qualifications is preferred
